citation: van Campen C, Rowe PC, Visser FC. Two Different Hemodynamic Responses in ME/CFS Patients with Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome During Head-Up Tilt Testing. J Clin Med. 2024;13(24):7726.
protocol: Head-up tilt test to 70 degrees: supine rest before tilt (about 20 min in Methods), then tilted; supine and end-tilt values are compared. Healthy-control values are mid-tilt images from an earlier study of the same group.
population: 47 healthy controls (10 male, 37 female), age 38 +/- 14 y, BMI median 24.2 (IQR 21.3-27.3), recruited separately from the ME/CFS groups.

reports.where: Table 2, supine HR row, healthy-control column
Table 2, supine SBP row, healthy-control column

note: Table 2 cells are "mean (SD)" by the methods, with no label in the cells. The healthy-control supine values come from an earlier cohort, and the supine length for them is not restated.
